text:
The Canucks spent the first 13 minutes at Rogers Arena watching a game happen to them. Frank Nazar scored 35 seconds in, Tyler Bertuzzi and Roman Kantserov added power-play goals, and Dominic Toninato tipped in the fourth at 12:44. As Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis put it: "It was 4-0 for the Blackhawks before the #Canucks even had a shot on goal." Chicago, playing without captain Connor Bedard, who was placed on injured reserve ahead of shoulder surgery, did not look like a team feeling sorry for itself.

Kantserov was the night. The rookie, a 2023 second-round pick who scored 36 goals in the KHL last season, finished with three goals and an assist in 13:36, two of them on the power play. His tip-in at 12:56 of the second restored a three-goal lead, and his third-period wrister made it 6-3. Bertuzzi had a goal and two assists, Patrick Kane two assists, and Chicago went 3 for 4 with the extra man while Vancouver went 0 for 5.

Here is the part the score hides. Vancouver actually had the better chances overall, 3.59 expected goals to 3.43 (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and owned the second period 2.44 to 0.76. Zeev Buium's slap shot, a 3% chance, got the Canucks on the board, Filip Chytil cut it to 4-2, and Jake DeBrusk made it 5-3 after Kantserov's second. Brock Boeser missed the net on a 38% look in the middle frame. Our replays of every shot gave Vancouver a 53% chance to win this game, which tells you how much of it came down to special teams and the opening barrage.

In net, Nikita Tolopilo was charged with four goals on 11 shots, 3.03 more than those chances deserved. Kevin Lankinen stopped 17 of 19. At the other end, Drew Commesso made 22 saves on 25 shots, 0.59 better than expected, and topped our list of wins added, including a stop on DeBrusk late in the second period with Chicago up two.

For Vancouver, already without Elias Pettersson (upper body) and a day removed from a shootout win over Minnesota, a 0-for-5 power play against a team missing its best player is the kind of night that stings. For Chicago, Mark Lazerus of The Athletic summed it up: "Power play stays red hot."
headline: Kantserov's hat trick and a power play buries Vancouver
